Microsoft Entra Workload ID
Each object that interacts with Microsoft Entra ID has an identity. Each user, device,
application, service, script, or container has an identity that identifies it uniquely in the
directory. This identity is used to authenticate to the directory and access other services and
resources. The terminology used for these identities varies across the industry. In Microsoft
Entra, a Workload ID refers to a digital identity that represents a non-human entity, such as an
application, service, script, or automation running in your environment. Unlike traditional
user accounts, which are tied to individual people, Workload IDs are created for resources and
workloads that need to authenticate and access resources programmatically. These identities
help organizations securely manage and control how their applications and automated
processes interact with other resources within Microsoft Entra, Azure, and integrated services.
Microsoft Entra Workload ID makes it easier to automate processes and maintain strong
security practices. It supports auditing, monitoring, and compliance efforts, as every action
taken by a workload is tracked and can be reviewed. This is particularly important in complex
cloud environments where automation and scalability are key.
In this chapter, we will cover
Applications in Microsoft Entra
Managed identities in Azure
Introduction to workload identities
Workload identity federation
Security for workload identities
Applications in Microsoft Entra
Most applications require idx_0e5013ee users to authenticate to be able to access them. Application
developers often don't want to store and manage user credentials in the application as this
•
•
•
•
•
introduces a lot of administrative overhead and security concerns. They would rather want to
delegate the identity and access management functions idx_5780c25e to an Identity Provider (IdP) like
Microsoft Entra ID.
There are several ways to use applications in Microsoft Entra. Before learning about workload
identities, it is important to understand the application types and their behavior.
In Microsoft Entra App Gallery, there are SaaS applications that can be added for use in your
tenant. These are applications like Box, Salesforce, ServiceNow etc. These applications are
published in the application owner's tenant like Box or Salesforce. This is the application's
home tenant. They can be added to your tenant for use by users in your organization. This can
be done in the Microsoft Entra admin center by navigating to Entra ID | Enterprise apps |
New application.
In addition, you can also register an application that your organization is developing. These are
your line-of-business (LOB) applications. This can be done in the Microsoft Entra admin center
by navigating to Entra ID | App registration | New application.

Managed identities for Azure resources
Applications use a variety idx_986da95a of secrets like credentials, certificates, and keys. Developers often
face challenges with secure handling of these secrets. Manually idx_19a642f4 managing these secrets in the
application is prone to errors and security issues. This is where managed identities help. A
managed identity is defined as an identity assigned to Azure resources like Azure Virtual
Machines, Service Fabric Clusters, Azure Kubernetes clusters, or any app hosting platform
supported by Azure. Once a managed identity is assigned to a compute resource, it can be
authorized to access other Azure resources like storage accounts, SQL databases and more.
Managed identities replace secrets like access keys, passwords, certificates, and other forms of
service-to-service authentication dependencies.
Using managed identities eliminates the need to manage credentials. They can be used to
authenticate any resource that supports Microsoft Entra authentication.
Managed identities are of two types.
System-assigned: Some Azure idx_6718f5c2 resources enable the creation of managed identities
directly from the resource. When a system-assigned managed identity is enabled, a
service principal representing the managed identity is created in Microsoft Entra. It is
tied to the resource and if the Azure resource is deleted, the service principal is also
deleted.
User-assigned: A user-assigned identity is an independent identity that can be
assigned to Azure resources if they don't support system-assigned managed identity.
When a user-assigned managed identity is created, a service principal representing it is
created in Microsoft Entra. This service principal is not tied to the Azure resource and
•
•

must be managed separately. These can be used in workload identity federation
scenarios.
Introduction to workload identities
There are two main idx_7865403c types of identities – human or non-human/machine identities. Human
identities are idx_9308f17a the ones that are assigned idx_89d6262a to individuals idx_b888ef11 like employees, vendors, business
partners, or customers. Non-human/machine identities consist of workload identities and
device identities. Device identities represent devices like computers, mobile devices or IoT
devices. Workload identities are assigned to software like an application or service. In

Microsoft Entra, workload identities refer to applications, service principals and managed
identities. Let's understand each one in detail.
Applications and service principals
Using applications in Microsoft Entra as described in Table 11.1 creates an identity configuration
for the application that allows it to use Microsoft Entra ID as its IdP. Once the application is
added or registered with Microsoft Entra ID, a globally unique instance of the application is
created in the tenant. This instance idx_6feaa5b8 has an App/Client ID that is globally unique. Secrets and
certificates can be added to make the application work. Registering or adding an application
creates an application object and a service principal object in the tenant.
Application object
Each application idx_c614ed1b in Microsoft idx_d1d577cd Entra is defined by its unique application object that is created
when the application is registered or added to the tenant. These application objects can be
viewed in the Microsoft Entra admin center by navigating to Entra ID | App registrations | All
applications as shown in the following screenshot.
Figure 11.1: Application objects

chunks.title: masteringmicrosoftentraid
chunks.heading: Chapter 11 380

The application object describes how the IdP issues tokens for application access, the resources
that need access to the idx_f622dd3d application and the actions that the application can take.
Service principal object
To access resources idx_a14a7538 secured by Microsoft Entra, the entity requiring idx_7bda2901 access must be represented
by a security principal. Users are represented by user principal and applications are
represented by service principals. These security principals define the access and permissions
that users and applications have in the Microsoft Entra tenant. This enables authentication
and authorization for the users or applications when they attempt to access resources. There
are three types of service principal:
Applications: These are local representations or instances of global applications in
your tenant. It is created from an application object and inherits certain properties
from the application object. A service principal is created in each tenant where the
application is used and defines what the application can do in that tenant, who can
access the application and the resources that the application can access.
Managed identity: This type of service principal represents a managed identity in
Azure. When a managed identity is enabled in Azure, a managed identity service
principal object is created in Microsoft Entra. These service principals can be granted
access and permissions, but they cannot be updated or modified. Unlike application
service principals, they do not have an application object associated with them.
Legacy: These are service principals that were created before app registrations were
introduced or when an app is created using legacy methods. They can have credentials,
service principal names, reply URLs, and other properties. They don't have an
associated app registration. Legacy service principals can only be used in the tenant
where they were created.
You can view the service principal objects in the Microsoft Entra admin center by navigating to
Entra ID | Enterprise apps | All applications as shown in the following screenshot:
•
•

Figure 11.2: Service principal objects
To summarize, an application object is a global representation or master copy of the
application and can be viewed under App registrations (Figure 11.1). It defines what the
application is (its identity, permissions, endpoints, and configuration). A service principal
object is the local representation of the application and can be viewed under Enterprise apps
(Figure 11.2). It defines how the app runs in your tenant (assignments, policies, access control).
Each software application is represented by a single application object in the tenant. An
application object can have multiple service principals associated with it as a service principal

must be created in each tenant where the application is used.
In the world of AI, an increasing number of services rely on non-human identities to complete
tasks. The number of non-human identities is increasing dramatically. Adversaries are
targeting these non-human identities, putting applications and the organization's resources at
risk. Unlike human identities, non-human identities often lack a formal lifecycle or governance
process. It is difficult to track the creation of these identities, making it difficult to govern them
and decide when to revoke them. Most identity and access management solutions focus on
protecting human idx_04d00712 identities. Microsoft Entra Workload idx_5aa358f5 ID helps address the same concerns for
workload identities.
Using Microsoft Entra Workload ID, organizations can
Bring service principals idx_ae1f63cb under the purview of Conditional Access policies.
Enforce Conditional Access location and risk policies using Continuous Access
Evaluation.
Detect threats and reduce risk to workload identities by using Microsoft Entra ID
Protection.

Chapter 11 382
Use managed identities to access Microsoft Entra protected resources without
needing to manage secrets for resources that run on Azure.
Use workload identity federation to access Microsoft Entra protected resources in
scenarios like GitHub Actions, workloads running on Kubernetes and on non-Azure
platforms without needing to manage secrets.
Use access review for service principals to manage service principals and
applications that idx_b3f403bc are assigned privileged directory roles in Microsoft Entra ID. Access
reviews are explained in detail in Chapter 6, Microsoft Entra Entitlement Management.
Let's explore idx_1511e769 each of these capabilities in detail.
Workload identity federation
Software applications need an idx_8d1faeeb identity for authentication and to access and communicate with
other resources. If these workloads are running on Azure, you can use managed identities to
manage the secrets and provide secure access to Microsoft Entra resources. Workloads running
in Kubernetes or non-Azure platforms use application credentials like client secrets or
certificates to authenticate to and access Microsoft Entra resources. These application
credentials pose a security risk and must be stored securely and properly protected. They
should also be regularly rotated. If expired, they can also cause application downtime.
Workload identity federation enables such workloads to securely access Microsoft Entra
resources without having to idx_50523180 manage secrets. This can be done by configuring a user-assigned
managed identity or using app registration in Microsoft Entra ID, which idx_eb45f124 creates a trust
between Entra ID and an external IdP like GitHub or Google. For applications, this is done by
configuring federated identity credentials (FIC). Once this idx_c80842c7 trust relationship is established,
the external software workload sends trusted tokens from the external IdP to the Microsoft
identity platform and receives an access token in return. The access token is then used by the
software to access Microsoft Entra resources. There is a limit of 20 federated identity
credentials per application object or user-assigned identity.
The following figure explains how workload identity federation works.
•
•
•
383 Microsoft Entra Workload ID
Figure 11.3: Workload identity federation
Using workload identity federation, workloads running on any Kubernetes cluster, Amazon
Web Services (AWS), or other cloud platform, GitHub Actions, Google Cloud, and more can
securely access resources protected by Microsoft Entra without having to manage secrets.
A federated identity idx_3f347d68 credential is made up of the following:
audiences: This is the audience that appears in the token
issuer: This is the URL of the external IdP
subject: This is the identifier of the software workload in the external IdP

chunks.title: masteringmicrosoftentraid
chunks.heading: Chapter 11 382
chunks.content:
name: This is a string that uniquely identifies the credential
The issuer and subject combination must be unique for the app. When the external software
workload requests the Microsoft identity platform for an access token in exchange for the
external token, the Microsoft identity platform checks the issuer and subject values of the
federated identity credential against the issuer and subject claims in the external token. If
the values match, an access token is issued.
Currently federated identity credentials require explicit matching when comparing subject,
issuer and audience in the federated identity credential to subject, issuer and audience
claims in the external token sent to Microsoft Entra ID. Considering that only 20 federated
identity credentials can be created for a single application or user-assigned identity, this can
lead to scaling issues. For applications, flexible federated identity credentials extend the
capabilities of the existing federated identity credentials by allowing the use of a restricted
expression language for matching the incoming subject claims. They also enable including
custom claims, thereby extending the federated identity credential model beyond the subject,
issuer and audience claims. This enables multiple federated identity credentials to be
managed under a single flexible federated identity credential. These include scenarios like

To configure a idx_912bc1b5 federated idx_6914b9c8 identity credential, you must be the owner of the application or have
one of the following idx_d01157d6 Entra roles: Application Administrator, Cloud Application
Administrator, Global Administrator or Hybrid Identity Administrator.
The following are the steps to configure a federated identity credential:
Create an app registration or managed identity in Microsoft Entra. Grant the app access

From the App registration blade in the Microsoft Entra admin center, find and record

From the external software workload, obtain the subject and issuer information.
Log in to https://entra.microsoft.com and navigate to Entra ID | App
registrations.
Select the app registration created in step 1 and click on Certificates & secrets.
In the right pane, click on Federated credentials, then click Add credential.
From the Federated credential scenario drop-down, select the scenario for which you
are adding the credential. Refer to the following screenshot:

Securing workload identities
As can be understood by idx_8353fe8a now, workload identities differ from user identities in that they often
do not have a proper lifecycle. They also need to store their secrets somewhere and cannot
perform multifactor authentication. These differences make workload identities more
susceptible to compromise and harder to protect.
Microsoft Entra ID Protection can be used to provide detection, investigation, and
remediation services for applications and service principals. The following risk detections are
available for workload identities.
Microsoft Entra threat intelligence: This detection indicates some activity that is
consistent with known attack patterns.
Suspicious sign-ins: Detects sign-in properties that are unusual for the service
principal. It learns and baselines behavior over 2 and 60 days and then generates an
alert if unfamiliar properties like IP address, user agent, IP country are detected at
subsequent sign-ins.

Chapter 11 390
Continuous Access Evaluation for workload identities
Continuous Access Evaluation (CAE) for idx_af6719fd workload idx_785f8f6e identities improves security by enforcing
Conditional Access location and risk policies in real time and instantly revokes the token if risk
is identified. The following points must be kept in mind while using CAE for workload
identities.
CAE for workload identities is only supported on access requests sent to Microsoft
Graph as the resource provider.
Service principals for line-of-business applications are supported.
Revocation events supported are:
Disable a service principal
Delete a service principal
High service principal risk
Developers need to enable their application to opt in to CAE for workload identities. This can
be done by declaring the cp1 client capability in their API call when requesting tokens.
When CAE is triggered idx_af8ed8f3 and a client's session idx_2f3dee81 is revoked, the client must reauthenticate. This
behavior can be verified from the sign-in logs.
Best practices
Following are some best idx_d4f73e10 practices for working with Microsoft Entra Workload ID.
Use managed identities wherever possible to avoid storing secrets.
Prefer workload identity federation to eliminate long-lived credentials.
Enforce least-privilege access using Privileged Identity Management for workload
roles.
Review permissions regularly. Use Microsoft Entra Access Reviews for App roles and
service principals.
Use Microsoft Entra Recommendations to identify expiring client secrets and rotate
them before expiry to prevent application outages.
Automate provisioning and deprovisioning to maintain lifecycle hygiene.
Apply Conditional Access policies tailored for workload identities.
Continuously monitor sign-ins, audit logs, and permission changes.

seamless access across diverse external scenarios.

In today's interconnected world, organizations cannot operate in silos. They need to
collaborate with external entities like contractors, partners, vendors, and consumers. External
identities refer to these users or entities outside an organization's core workforce who require
access to the organization's resources, systems, or applications. These may include partners,
suppliers, contractors, customers, or external consultants. Managing external identities
efficiently is crucial for maintaining security and collaboration while ensuring that only the
right individuals are granted the appropriate level of access.
External identities idx_c6879d57 can be managed using Microsoft Entra. It supports business-to-business
(B2B) collaboration, which allows external users to authenticate using their home credentials,
reducing the administrative overhead of creating and idx_8f53e75f maintaining separate accounts.
Microsoft Entra also offers a Consumer Identity and Access Management (CIAM) solution,
which is used to manage consumer identities. Conditional Access policies can be applied to
external identities, ensuring that access is granted only under specific conditions, such as from
trusted locations or devices.
Monitoring and auditing tools are also essential, providing visibility into how external
identities interact with organizational resources and enabling timely responses to suspicious
activity. A robust strategy for managing external identities balances security, compliance, and
productivity.
This chapter will cover
Introduction to Microsoft Entra External ID
External ID in the workforce tenant
•
•
Identity providers
Governance and ID Protection
Introduction to Microsoft Entra External ID
Microsoft Entra External ID is a comprehensive identity management solution designed to
help organizations idx_b5d82317 securely collaborate and interact with users outside their immediate
workforce. As businesses increasingly operate in a global, interconnected environment, the
need to seamlessly engage partners, suppliers, contractors, and customers without
compromising security has become paramount. Microsoft Entra External ID addresses this
challenge by providing a unified platform for managing external identities, streamlining
access, and enforcing robust security policies.
At its core, Microsoft Entra External ID enables organizations to extend their digital ecosystem
beyond traditional boundaries. By leveraging B2B collaboration features, external users can
access resources using their own existing credentials from their home organizations or even
social identity providers. This federated approach reduces the administrative burden of
maintaining separate accounts for every external user and enhances the user experience by

chunks.title: masteringmicrosoftentraid
chunks.heading: Chapter 15, Microsoft Entra Private Access
chunks.content:
allowing individuals to use familiar sign-in methods.
A key advantage of Entra External ID is its support for CIAM. This functionality is particularly
valuable for organizations with customer-facing applications or services. CIAM allows
businesses to create secure, branded sign-up and sign-in experiences for customers, enabling
them to register with email addresses or social accounts. Organizations can customize the user
journey, including MFA and consent management, all while maintaining compliance with data
protection regulations.
Security is central to the design of Microsoft Entra External ID. Organizations can apply
Conditional Access policies specifically tailored to external identities. These policies ensure
that access to sensitive resources is granted only under predefined conditions, such as from
trusted networks, compliant devices, or after satisfying MFA requirements. For example, a
contractor working remotely might be required to authenticate using MFA and access certain
systems only from approved locations. These granular controls help mitigate risks associated
with external access while still enabling productivity.
Another critical aspect of managing external identities is governance. Microsoft Entra External
ID provides comprehensive tools for monitoring, auditing, and managing the lifecycle of
external accounts. Administrators can track how external users interact with organizational
resources, identify suspicious activities, and enforce timely removal of access when a
partnership or contract ends. Automated workflows and access reviews streamline the process
•
•

chunks.content:
Chapter 12 398
of ensuring that only authorized individuals retain access, reducing the risk of lingering or
orphaned accounts.
Entra External ID also supports cross-tenant access settings, allowing organizations to define
which external tenants can collaborate with their users and which resources are accessible.
This feature is particularly useful in scenarios where regulatory compliance or internal policies
mandate strict boundaries between different business units or external partners. By enforcing
these restrictions, organizations can prevent data leakage and maintain greater control over
their digital assets.
Integration with idx_3ab069b0 other Microsoft Entra features, such as identity protection and continuous
access evaluation, further enhances the security posture. These capabilities enable real-time
risk assessment and dynamic policy enforcement, adapting to changing threat landscapes and
user behaviors. For example, if an external user's account is compromised, Entra can
automatically trigger additional verification steps or block access until the risk is resolved.
Microsoft Entra External ID primarily caters to the following two scenarios:
Business-to-consumer: This is for organizations developing consumer-facing
applications idx_a43c3699 like an online idx_a889b020 grocery store, website for booking air tickets or government
departments offering citizen-facing services. These types of applications can use Entra
External ID in external configuration. This is a separate tenant from the one that
contains the organization's employees.
Business-to-business: This idx_b106c238 is for organizations idx_ece5f8cd that need to collaborate with other
businesses like partners, vendors, suppliers, etc. They can use Entra External ID in
workforce configuration which is the same tenant that contains the organization's
employees.
Most organizations have both business-to-business and business-to-consumer requirements,
and you will find that they have both external and workforce tenant configurations in Microsoft
Entra.
Before moving on, let's learn a little more about external and workforce tenant configurations.
A tenant in Microsoft Entra is a directory that contains the organization's employees and
resources like applications and devices. In Microsoft Entra, a tenant can be configured in two
ways depending on the use case.
Workforce tenant: A workforce tenant is the standard configuration in Microsoft
Entra. It idx_8b4683cb contains the organization's employees, business applications, devices, and
other resources. In a workforce tenant, the users are the organization's employees.

Identity providers
An identity provider (IdP) is a service that authenticates and verifies the identity of users,
allowing them idx_01f6ed68 to access applications and resources across different systems. Microsoft Entra
ID is an IdP that provides such services. When you invite external users to collaborate with
your organization, they may already have an identity in another Microsoft Entra tenant, or a
Microsoft Account or a social account like Google or Facebook. External ID in the workforce
tenant offers collaboration with other IdPs like
Other Microsoft Entra accounts: Invited users can use their own Microsoft Entra
accounts from their home tenants to access resources in your tenant. This is enabled by
default and if an external user has a Microsoft Entra account, they can redeem your B2B
invitation using that account. Just invite the user using the normal invitation flow.
Microsoft accounts (MSA): Microsoft accounts are consumer accounts, set up by users
to access services like Hotmail, Outlook, Xbox etc. Guest users can use their personal
MSA to redeem B2B invitations and access resources in your tenant. This is enabled by
default and if an external user has an existing MSA, they can redeem your B2B
invitation using that account. Just invite the user using the normal invitation flow.
Email one-time passcode: With this option a guest user can redeem an invitation
using an email OTP. Each time they try to access a resource in your tenant, they will
receive an OTP which they use to authenticate. This is enabled by default and can be
used in user flow. Creating user flows is explained in Chapter 13, External Identities in
External Tenants.
Social identities: Microsoft Entra supports federation with social identity providers
such idx_54d3c62b as Google and Facebook. Users can redeem invitations and access resources in
your tenant using Google credentials. Facebook federation, however, is supported only
for self-service sign-up user flows and cannot be used to redeem invitations.
Federation with Google and Facebook can be configured in the Microsoft Entra admin
center by navigating to Entra ID | External identities | All identity providers.
SAML/WS-Fed identity provider federation: Organizations can also set up federation
with any external IdP that supports SAML or WS-Fed protocols. This federation allows
users to use their own credentials to access resources in your tenant. This can be
configured in the Microsoft Entra admin center by navigating to Entra ID | External
identities | All identity providers | Custom.
By leveraging these identity providers, organizations can collaborate with external users
without having to manage their credentials.

Cross-tenant access settings
Cross-tenant idx_5a2e24d4 access settings are used to manage B2B collaboration with other Microsoft Entra

can control the outbound and inbound B2B collaboration with other organizations using
cross-tenant access settings. These settings allow administrators to manage how their
organization interacts with other Microsoft Entra tenants.
In Microsoft Entra, a resource tenant is the inviting tenant. For example, if you are inviting
external users to access resources in your tenant, then your tenant becomes the resource
tenant. The tenant where the guest user's identity originates and is managed is called the
user's home tenant.

B2B direct connect
B2B direct connect is a feature that allows organizations to set up a mutual trust relationship
with another idx_29861a46 Microsoft Entra organization. Currently, this feature only supports Microsoft
Teams shared channels. With this feature enabled, users idx_0abc696f from both organizations can
collaborate in a shared Teams channel using their home credentials. They don't have to be
added to each other's organizations as guests.
For B2B direct connect to work, both tenants must establish mutual trust by enabling the
required inbound access settings for each other. Because the trust is configured as an inbound
setting, each organization must enable it on their own tenant. B2B direct connect only works
when both tenants are in the same Microsoft cloud environment. Refer to Figure 12.9. Then
users in one organization can create a Microsoft Teams shared channel and invite users from
the other organization. The invited user can access the shared channel from within Teams in

ID Protection for B2B users
Using idx_0737db4b Microsoft Entra ID Protection, organizations can block users from signing in if their
credentials are considered at risk. Microsoft Entra ID Protection detects compromised
credentials for B2B users. The user risk for B2B users is evaluated in their home tenant. When
these users try to access resources in the resource tenant, their real-time sign-in risk is
calculated. Microsoft Entra ID Protection can then enforce risk-based Conditional Access
policies for B2B users. Risk-based Conditional Access policies are explained in Chapter 9,
Microsoft Entra ID Protection.
The following idx_232a0d16 ID Protection limitations apply to B2B users:
If the user risk policy is triggered and a password reset is required, the user will be
blocked. This is because the user's password is maintained in their home directory and
not the resource directory.
Guest users do not show up in the risky users report. This is because user risk for guest
users is evaluated in their home directory.
Administrators in the resource directory cannot dismiss a user risk or remediate risk for
a B2B user because the user object is maintained in the user's home directory.
It is recommended to use Microsoft Entra ID Protection for B2B users to protect your tenant
even if the user's home tenant has not enabled ID protection.
